items.excerpt: Across the Americas, Guatemala is investigating the killing of a prominent anti-corruption lawyer, while a deadly Jamaican police operation raises questions about accountability. Brazil reports a historic decline in Amazon deforestation, Peru declares a fishing emergency linked to El Niño, and Colombia's new embassy in Jerusalem signals a significant diplomatic shift. In Asia-Pacific, China is tightening oversight of technology exports, while Australia faces political divisions over its proposed European trade agreement. New Zealand continues losing citizens despite positive overall migration, Japan is reassessing Pacific surveillance capabilities, and South Korea is challenging American proposals affecting wartime military command. In Africa, Somalia advances legislation against female genital mutilation, while Egypt reports improving Suez Canal traffic despite continuing shipping disruptions. Middle Eastern tensions remain high as Saudi Arabia intercepts renewed missile and drone attacks, Washington intensifies maritime and financial pressure on Iran, and an attack involving European diplomats in the West Bank prompts international concern. Across Europe, France faces widespread protests over living costs and public services, Italy's steel crisis threatens thousands of jobs, and Spain's divided left prepares for November's election. Portugal has selected Lufthansa for a major stake in TAP, while Britain examines Microsoft's position in emerging artificial intelligence markets. Greenland is defending control over its natural resources, Germany is considering special borrowing arrangements for Ukraine assistance, and Norway is debating changes to its sovereign wealth fund's ethical investment rules. ... Elsewhere, Iceland is preparing for potentially severe Atlantic climate disruption, Uzbekistan is planning additional nuclear power plants, and Bangladesh is reviewing its vaccination system amid a major measles outbreak. ... Finally, Ukraine reports restrictions affecting satellite-connected defensive drones, exposing its dependence on foreign-controlled battlefield technology.

items.title: Inflation is retreating from most of the store — why your biggest bills are the holdouts: Chart of the Day
items.excerpt: Inflation is retreating from most of the store — why your biggest bills are the holdouts: Chart of the Day # Inflation is retreating from most of the store — why your biggest bills are the holdouts: Chart of the Day Jared Blikre Sun, October 18, 2026 at 6:33 AM CDT 3 min read Inflation is reaching fewer corners of the economy. That doesn't mean life is getting cheaper. Only about 38% of the roughly 175 categories in the Consumer Price Index rose faster than a 3% annual pace over the past six months, according to Yahoo Finance calculations from Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) data. That's down from 56% in May and the fewest since spring 2025. The count borrows a test from Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh, who laid it out at Jackson Hole in August. He counts how many categories in the Fed's preferred PCE price gauge are rising faster than 3%, a gauge of how widespread inflation is. The Fed's goal is still 2%. BLS, Yahoo Finance "Too many categories are still posting increases above 3% on both a six- and 12-month basis," Warsh said after the Fed raised rates in September. By that yardstick, September looked better than its hotter-than-expected headline. The 12-month count slipped to about 47% from 51% in August. At the 2022 peak, about 4 in 5 categories topped 3%. In the two decades before the pandemic, about 1 in 3 typically did. A narrower spread strengthens the case for waiting, and traders have leaned that way. The bond market put the odds of a hike at the Oct. 27-28 meeting at about 17% by Friday's close, according to Bloomberg data — down from roughly 33% after Wednesday's CPI report. Warsh declined to preview his next move in remarks Friday before the International Monetary Fund. Some Fed officials want more evidence before moving. Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee called September's inflation report discouraging but told Yahoo Finance's Jennifer Schonberger he favors waiting before acting again. "We need to get more data," he said. ## The holdout categories are the expensive ones Electricity, rent, hospital services, and car repairs have all been rising faster than 3% over the past six months, after adjusting for seasonal swings. Gasoline is up about 34% from a year ago. Together, the categories still above the line make up at least 60% of the CPI basket, which the BLS weights by how much households spend on each item. Groceries show the other side of the problem. Grocery prices rose less than 2% over the past year, yet they're still up nearly a third since December 2019. items.title: Texas Democrats eye breakthrough as Republicans face ...
items.excerpt: After more than three decades of Republican dominance, Democrats in Texas see a rare chance to break through in November's midterm elections, as voter anger over immigration raids and the cost of living tests US President Donald Trump's support. No Democrat has won statewide office in the conservative southern state since 1994, and Trump carried Texas by nearly 14 percentage points in the 2024 presidential election. ... But with a US Senate seat and the governorship at stake on November 3, recent polls suggest Republicans face an unusually competitive challenge. ... At the forefront is James Talarico, a 37-year-old former teacher and state lawmaker whose blend of Christian faith, economic populism and appeals for political unity has helped make the Senate race one of the country's most closely watched. ... A University of Texas poll released this week put Talarico ahead of Republican Ken Paxton, the state's attorney general and a staunch Trump ally, by 50 percent to 47 percent -- a lead within the survey's margin of error. A separate UMass Lowell poll found the two candidates tied. ... Trump, however, has campaigned aggressively for Paxton, warning at a recent rally in San Antonio that losing the seat could jeopardize the Republicans' narrow Senate majority.

items.title: Trump endorses embattled Israeli PM Netanyahu for reelection : NPR
items.excerpt: WEST PALM BEACH, Fla. — President Donald Trump on Sunday endorsed embattled Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu late in his reelection campaign, a coveted boost because of Trump's popularity but one that the American had withheld for months as the vote neared and the leaders' strategies in the Middle East diverged. ... Trump said in a post on social media that Netanyahu "has been a Great Warrior Prime Minister, and an even greater Partner for Peace in combatting the Islamic Republic of Iran." ... Israelis are set to vote Oct. 27, in the first national elections since Hamas attacked Israel on Oct. 7, 2023. ... The absence of an endorsement was a setback for the Likud politician, who had billed his tight ties to the Republican president as a selling point for staying in power. ... It was not immediately clear what impact the endorsement would have on what is expected to be a tight race. Trump is still popular in Israel, but many Israelis, including leading commentators, have expressed disappointment over the inconclusive outcome of the Iran war and Trump's ceasefire proposal, which fell short of many of the countries' key goals when they jointly launched the war in February. ... In his post, Trump again threatened to "soon finish the job" against Iran "unless they change their ways, rapidly," but added he might not want to if Netanyahu loses the election. "If Israel has the wrong Leader, which would be anyone other than Bibi, America will have to do this work ourselves, and I am not inclined to do so," Trump said.

This gives Democrats a substantial edge on major issues like the economy and healthcare. Grass fire at Canadian military base kills 4 soldiers and critically injures 19 other people WAINWRIGHT, Alberta (AP) — A grass fire killed four Canadian service members and injured 39 other people, 19 of them critically, as it swept through a military training area where soldiers were using live ammunition. Military officials believed the fire was contained enough to allow the training on an Alberta base to continue Saturday. But the winds suddenly shifted, and military officials said the flames were upon them in less than a minute. Prime Minister Mark Carney described the fire as one of the worst peacetime tragedies for Canada’s military on domestic soil. He ordered flags lowered to half-staff on federal buildings nationwide. Jeffries likes Democrats' chances in race for the House as he campaigns in Ohio TOLEDO, Ohio (AP) — House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries says the election climate is holding firm for Democrats as they race to retake the House. Jeffries campaigned Sunday for Rep. Marcy Kaptur in a heavily contested Ohio congressional district that is crucial for majority control. He also slapped back at President Donald Trump’s abrupt decision to waive sanctions on Russia. Jeffries, who is in line to become House speaker if Democrats seize the majority, has traveled to some 50 cities campaigning for Democratic candidates. The Toledo-area seat has been held by Kaptur for decades. But Trump has carried the district and Republicans are trying to flip it. Protests against rising living costs and poor school conditions have led to clashes with police and looting, resulting in at least 1,800 arrests across the country. Macron blamed radical far-left groups and criminals. He held an emergency meeting with officials and instructed measures to protect public buildings. items.excerpt: Updated: Monday, October 19, 2026, 10:26 [IST] ... Entertainment News Live Updates Today In India (October 19, 2026): Monday blues are hitting harder than ever following the shocking Juhu firing incident. Amid the festive spirit of Durga Puja and Navratri, the entertainment world is buzzing with fresh updates, celebrity news and major developments you won't want to miss. ... To begin with, Sunday evening took a shocking turn after multiple rounds of gunfire were reported at Tiger Shroff's car in Juhu. Fortunately, the actor did not sustain any gunshot injuries. Following the alarming incident, Disha Patani was reportedly spotted rushing to Tiger's residence last night to meet her rumoured ex-boyfriend. Rajinikanth's Jailer 2 has enjoyed a strong opening weekend at the box office, registering an impressive performance both in India and overseas. The sequel has witnessed a significant surge in its worldwide earnings, reportedly nearing the ₹425 crore mark within just four days of release. ... ## Tiger Shroff Firing Case: All 3 Shooters Arrested In Kota Police have arrested all three suspects linked to the firing incident involving Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff in Rajasthan’s Kota. The accused reportedly include a 17-year-old boy and a 22-year-old man employed as a Rapido rider in Mumbai. The Anti-Gangster Task Force, working alongside Rajasthan Police, detained the trio near Kota railway station after they allegedly escaped Mumbai following the incident. ... ## Tiger Shroff Firing: FIR Lodged Against 3 Unidentified Persons The Mumbai Police have registered a case of attempt to murder against three unidentified persons in connection with the firing at Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff's car, officials said on Monday. The case, initially registered by the Juhu police, has been transferred to the Mumbai Crime Branch in view of the seriousness of the offence, they said. Unidentified assailants opened fire at Shroff's car in Mumbai's Juhu area on Sunday evening. The actor escaped unhurt, while his driver and another person were injured. ... ## Jailer 2 Opening Weekend Worldwide Box Office Collection: Rajinikanth's Film Nears XXX Cr Mark Globally Rajinikanth's Jailer 2 continued its strong box office run on Sunday, October 18, recording an increase in domestic net collections on its fourth day in theatres. The Tamil action comedy, which arrived in cinemas worldwide on October 15, has accumulated ₹199.90 crore in India net collections, according to Sacnilk. Its worldwide gross collection has reached ₹424.25 crore after four days. The film collected an estimated ₹55.85 crore net across India on Day 4, registering an 18.2% increase over Saturday's reported collection of ₹47.25 crore. Sunday's performance also took the film's total India gross to ₹234.25 crore. Overseas markets contributed another ₹40 crore on the fourth day, bringing the cumulative overseas gross to ₹190 crore. ... ## Disha Patani Rushes To Rumored Ex-BF Tiger Shroff's Residence After Shocking Firing Incident On Sunday, unidentified gunmen opened fire in Mumbai’s Juhu area, targeting a car linked to Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff. The actor did not sustain any gunshot injuries. Following the incident, a paparazzi video showed Disha Patani arriving at Tiger’s residence. Appearing visibly concerned, she reportedly ignored the photographers outside and hurried indoors to meet him. The two actors have been rumoured to have dated for several years, although neither has publicly confirmed their relationship.

items.excerpt: Two Nights! Getting Killed Again Tour ... ### Bill Orcutt Monday, October 19, 2026 Doors: 7:00 pm | Show: 8:00 pm Sold Out! ... ## Geese Ripping up the expected blueprint Geese set with their 2021 debut Projector and the cowboy rock follow-up of 2023’s 3D Country, Getting Killed puts the very idea of conventional rock structures in the band’s crosshairs. Working at a feverish clip with renowned producer Kenneth Blume over a month-long stretch, Geese emerged wielding a sharp, novel new vision for the genre, sporting wry smiles and a resolute confidence. The album was crowned the number one album of the year on numerous Best of 2025 lists including TIME, The New Yorker, The New York Times and more. The band began 2026 right where they left off, with an unwieldy, vexing SNL debut, a surprisingly intimate Tiny Desk concert and winning a BRIT Award for International Group of the Year.
